outcomes.description: Transform the image into a chalk drawing.

nodes.question: Does the edited image visibly have a chalk-like drawing medium or surface treatment?
nodes.criteria: pass: visible chalk-like marks or texture establish a chalk medium; fail: the image is clearly rendered in a non-chalk medium with no visible chalk treatment; unknown: the medium cannot be determined from the image.
nodes.binding: Assess only visible evidence that the image uses a chalk-like medium or treatment.

nodes.question: Does the edited image visibly present its depicted content as a drawing rather than as an unchanged photograph?
nodes.criteria: pass: visible rendering establishes a drawing, such as drawn or illustrated forms; fail: the depicted content remains clearly photographic with no visible drawing conversion; unknown: the image does not establish whether it is a drawing or photograph.
nodes.binding: Assess only whether the image has been rendered as a drawing; do not assess its medium.

nodes.question: Has the image been transformed into a drawing made from chalk?
nodes.criteria: Use only the saved statuses and image-grounded evidence from n1 and n2. complete: both supports pass, establishing both a chalk medium and a drawing. partial: at least one support passes, but the other fails, so some requested transformation is evidenced without complete fulfillment. absent: both supports fail, establishing neither requested feature. unknown: no support passes and at least one is unknown, leaving progress unresolved. A known failure is negative evidence, not uncertainty; do not infer facts beyond the support evidence. Unrelated edits do not count as progress.
nodes.binding: Target: the image. Reference: a drawing made from chalk. Combine the independent evidence for chalk medium and drawing form; do not inspect images or add requirements.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

rejected_diagnostics.semantic_rejection: The requested readout is not semantically sound. It treats one support failure as evidence that the corresponding requested feature is absent, and both failures as proof of no progress. But n1 and n2 only assess visible evidence under their criteria; a failure may not establish that the image has not been transformed in the requested way. The readout therefore overstates negative evidence and can return absent or partial without sufficient support. It also requires both supports to pass for completion, although their criteria do not establish that the whole image was converted into a chalk drawing. The program needs evidence that supports the requested extent, not merely chalk-like treatment and drawing form in isolation.

The requested readout is nested under n2, so it is activated only when n2 returns pass, fail, or unknown—which covers all allowed support statuses. However, its composition rules are contradictory: partial requires at least one support to pass, while unknown applies when no support passes and at least one is unknown; these conditions overlap when one support is unknown and the other fails. The program therefore does not define a unique readout for that evidence combination.

The support checks do not establish the requested extent reliably. n1 treats broad coverage of the main depicted content as evidence of progress but does not determine whether the whole image has been converted; n2 likewise allows a pass for drawing treatment across depicted content without defining or checking substantial unconverted areas consistently. The readout then permits complete when both supports pass and their evidence establishes broad treatment, so it can infer full-image conversion from coarse coverage. This fails the requirement that a coarse support pass not imply an unexamined finer condition.

The support checks cover chalk-like treatment and drawing form, but neither establishes whether the conversion applies to the image as a whole. The requested readout requires both supports to pass and their evidence to explicitly establish whole-image conversion, yet the supports do not collect that extent evidence. This leaves complete fulfillment unprovable even when both pass, so the program does not preserve the requested property and extent.

The requested readout requires evidence that the image as a whole was converted into a chalk drawing, but neither support check assesses whole-image coverage or remaining photographic areas. The readout cannot establish those facts from the saved observations, so its complete/partial criteria are unsupported. In addition, n3 treats both supports failing as absence, although failure only establishes that each specific cue was not established; the criteria themselves acknowledge that this does not prove no requested progress. The program therefore risks converting missing evidence into a negative result.

findings.source_phrase: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk
findings.question: Does the drawing-like rendering extend across the whole image, including the giraffes and background, rather than leaving substantial areas photographic or only applying a chalk-like overlay?
findings.criteria: Pass if the depicted content throughout the image is visibly rendered as a drawing; fail if substantial content remains photographic or the treatment is only a surface effect over otherwise photographic content; unknown if the extent cannot be determined.
findings.evidence: The edited image shows softened, sketch-like contours on the giraffes and a grainy, blurred treatment across the scene, but the saved observations do not separately assess whether the drawing conversion is consistent across the full image.
findings.rationale: The requested transformation applies to “the image.” The existing drawing check establishes a drawing-like appearance but does not explicitly investigate its extent; the chalk-texture check alone cannot establish whole-image conversion.
